title: Philadelphia Eagles vs. Chicago Bears Postgame Analysis: What Happened, What We Got Right and What We Learned

excerpt: Chicago Bears won 27-7. THE NUMBER LANDED AND THE REASONING DID NOT. This is the most dangerous result on this page, because it pays and teaches nothing. Nothing below should be read as EdgeDesk having understood this game.
seo_description: Chicago Bears beat Philadelphia Eagles 27-7. EdgeDesk’s number implied Chicago Bears +3 — win. 2 of 11 gradeable claims held up, 5 did not. Process grade: UNSOUND. Research, not picks.
model_status_note: THE NUMBER LANDED AND THE REASONING DID NOT. This is the most dangerous result on this page, because it pays and teaches nothing. Nothing below should be read as EdgeDesk having understood this game.

reasons: 5 of 9 gradeable claims went the other way. The read of this matchup was wrong in its mechanism, not only in its number.
The result carries 1 high-variance marker — a 3-turnover swing — so the scoreboard is weaker evidence than it looks.
EdgeDesk projected a home margin of 2.4 and the game finished 20 the home way — 17.6 points of margin error, inside the range the model published.
process.basis: the drivers, matchups and measured advantages only — never the price or the market claim, which are the result in longer words

variance_markers.label: A 3-turnover swing
variance_markers.text: Chicago Bears won the turnover battle by 3. Turnover margin is the least repeatable thing in football: it moves scoreboards hard and predicts almost nothing about the next meeting, so a result built on it says less about either team than the scoreline suggests.

verdict.line: THE NUMBER LANDED AND THE REASONING DID NOT. This is the most dangerous result on this page, because it pays and teaches nothing. Nothing below should be read as EdgeDesk having understood this game.

grading.separation_note: The bet result and the process grade above are computed separately and are allowed to disagree. A winning number with a broken thesis is recorded as exactly that.

lessons.actual_result: It graded a win. The reasoning behind it did not hold: 5 of 9 gradeable claims went the other way. The read of this matchup was wrong in its mechanism, not only in its number.
lessons.lesson: A winning number built on a reading the game contradicted. Nothing about this result should increase confidence in the mechanism EdgeDesk named, and treating it as confirmation is how a model gets worse while its record gets better.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Why did the number land while the mechanism failed? Either the number was right for a reason EdgeDesk has not identified, or it was luck. Both are worth knowing and they are different.

lessons.pregame_expectation: EdgeDesk makes it Chicago Bears -2.4 where the market has Chicago Bears +3.0 at BetOnline.ag — a 5.4 points disagreement.
lessons.actual_result: Chicago Bears won by 20. the result landed on EdgeDesk’s side of the market number: Chicago Bears beat a margin of -3
lessons.lesson: The disagreement landed. One landing proves nothing on its own; the aggregate of them, held against the closing line, is the only thing that would.
